name: CapCut Keyframe Spacing Control
use_when: A CapCut edit needs custom scale, position, rotation, color, overlay, or volume changes over time.
A built-in animation is too generic for the exact path, timing, or level change.
The agent needs to translate mobile CapCut keyframe behavior into structured ffmpeg, Remotion, Premiere, or DaVinci instructions.
A keyframed move has the correct start/end values but still feels robotic because the graph/easing curve is wrong.
Only one property should change over time, such as saturation, scale, position, filter strength, or music volume.
avoid_when: A simple built-in transition or animation already creates the needed movement cleanly.
The clip is already readable and movement would distract from speech, proof, or emotion.
The editor has not named what the keyframe change should help the viewer see, hear, or feel.

timeline_pattern.pattern: select_clip_or_overlay -> start_keyframe -> move_playhead -> change_property -> generated_keyframe -> preview_speed -> adjust_spacing_or_delete
timeline_pattern.spacing_rule: Keyframes closer together create faster changes; farther apart create slower, calmer changes.
timeline_pattern.property_rule: Treat keyframes as property-specific controls: a saturation keyframe should not imply hue or brightness changes unless those properties also have keyframes.
timeline_pattern.auto_keyframe_rule: After a first keyframe exists, changing the layer at a later playhead position can create or update the next keyframe automatically.
timeline_pattern.cleanup_rule: Delete wrong keyframes instead of leaving hidden drift or accidental values in the timeline.
timeline_pattern.built_in_rule: Use CapCut's animation button for simple standard entrances; use manual keyframes for custom paths or exact timing.
timeline_pattern.graph_rule: After start/end values are set, use Graphs to shape speed and flow between keyframes instead of relying on linear motion.

motion.rule: Pair scale with position when the focus target must stay readable.

keyframe_values.fast_social_move: Use close keyframes for snaps or dramatic moves only when the jolt is intentional.
keyframe_values.slow_move: Use wider spacing for slow zooms, gradual color shifts, or calm overlay movement.
keyframe_values.hold: Add a hold or duplicate-value keyframe when the viewer needs time to read the final state.
keyframe_values.quick_snap_spacing: A dramatic attention move can be only a few frames wide when the jolt is intentional; preview because the same values feel very different at 4 frames versus 20 frames.
keyframe_values.graph_slow_start: In the graph editor, a lower left-side curve creates a slower start.
keyframe_values.graph_fast_start: A higher left-side curve creates a faster start.
keyframe_values.graph_gentle_end: A lower right-side curve creates a gentler settle.
keyframe_values.graph_sharp_end: A higher right-side curve creates a sharper stop; use it only for intentional impact.

sound.rule: Use the same spacing logic for volume: short spacing creates quick ducks or rises, long spacing creates gradual fades.
sound.property_note: Audio volume keyframes should be judged by speech intelligibility, not by matching a visual spacing preset.

captions.rule: Check caption position after every scale, position, or rotation keyframe.

color.rule: Color keyframes should support a motivated mood or emphasis shift and preserve skin/proof readability.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent keyframes as timestamped property values for crop/scale/overlay/rotate/color/volume expressions; render short previews around every change.
implementation.remotion: Store keyframes as arrays of frame/value pairs per property and interpolate with a chosen easing function plus explicit hold frames.
implementation.blender: Use timeline keyframes on transform, material, color, or audio-strip volume and set interpolation deliberately.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Select the target clip/overlay/audio, add a starting keyframe, move the playhead, change the property, then use Graphs to shape start and end speed. Preview, adjust spacing/graph, or delete bad keyframes.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Effect Controls keyframes for Motion/Opacity/Color effects and audio rubber-band or clip volume keyframes; use temporal Bezier/Ease In/Ease Out when the move should not feel linear.

common_mistakes: Placing keyframes too close together and creating an accidental jolt.
Leaving unintended keyframes that cause drift after the move should stop.
Using manual keyframes for a simple entrance that a tested built-in animation handles faster.
Changing scale without position and losing the intended subject.
Changing the wrong property at the later playhead position and accidentally keyframing hue, brightness, scale, or position when only one property should move.
Animating before deciding the focus, audio, or mood job of the move.
Changing only keyframe spacing when the graph curve is what makes the move feel robotic.
Copying a graph preset to multiple clips without previewing each subject.
qc: Can the editor name the job of each keyframed property?
Does each property that changes have its own start and end keyframe?
Does keyframe spacing create the intended speed rather than accidental jolt or drag?
Does the graph curve create the intended start speed, acceleration, deceleration, and ending feel?
Are wrong or duplicate keyframes removed?
Does the final state hold long enough to read or hear?
Do captions, faces, proof, UI, and action remain safe through the full movement?
